title: Body of Evidence
blurb: Gross, weird and completely true facts about the thing you live in.

prompts.text: The three tiny bones in your middle ear are the hammer, the anvil and the _____.
The longest bone in the human body is the thigh bone, also called the _____.
Your cornea has no blood supply, so it takes its oxygen straight from the _____.
A baby's kneecaps start out as soft _____ and only slowly harden into bone over the first several years.
Your brain is about 2 percent of your body weight but burns roughly _____ percent of your energy.
Surgeons can operate on an awake patient's brain because brain tissue itself has no _____ receptors.
Identical twins share the same DNA but not their _____.
Your hair and fingernails are both made mostly of a protein called _____.
After surgery removes a big chunk of it, the _____ can regrow much of the lost tissue.
The thinnest skin on your body, under a millimetre thick, covers your _____.
A hiccup is a spasm of your _____ followed by your vocal cords snapping shut.
The funny bone is not a bone at all but the _____ nerve.
A red blood cell lives for about _____ days before it is recycled.
The medical name for earwax is _____.
The hardest substance in the human body is tooth _____.
Sweat itself is nearly odourless; the smell appears when _____ on your skin break it down.
Your left lung is smaller than your right to make room for your _____.
Your skin makes vitamin _____ when sunlight hits it.
Red blood cells are made inside your bones, in the soft tissue called bone _____.
An ice-cream headache happens when something cold hits the roof of your _____.
Your sense of balance depends on three fluid-filled loops in the inner ear called semicircular _____.
The pale half-moon at the base of a fingernail is called the _____.
Your tailbone has a medical name: the _____.
Children usually have _____ baby teeth.
The medical name for a rumbling stomach is _____.
The soft spots on a newborn's skull, where the bones haven't fused yet, are called _____.
Most people have _____ ribs.
The largest muscle in the human body by mass is the gluteus _____.
A full adult set of teeth, wisdom teeth included, is _____ teeth.
Colour vision depends on light-sensing cells in the retina called _____.
Most human cells carry _____ chromosomes.
The muscles that bend your fingers are mostly located in your _____.
Each human hand contains _____ bones.
Roughly a quarter of all the bones in your body are in your _____.
Each eye has a blind spot where the _____ nerve leaves the retina.
The first human heart transplant, in 1967, was performed in _____.
In 1980 the world declared the first human disease wiped out entirely: _____.
The stethoscope was invented in 1816 by a doctor who first used a rolled-up tube of _____.
The hormone nicknamed the hunger hormone, made mainly in your stomach, is called _____.
When it gets dark, your brain releases the sleep-timing hormone _____.
In the United States, the hormone adrenaline is usually called _____.
People who can't digest milk sugar lack an enzyme called _____.
Your gallbladder stores a digestive fluid made by the liver called _____.
In 1908 Kikunae Ikeda isolated the savoury taste umami from a broth made with the seaweed _____.
The smell of intestinal gas comes from tiny amounts of _____ compounds.
